## How Voice Dictation Changes the Writing Process


You have a clear idea in your head, but by the time you place your hands on the keyboard to draft a status update, the thought has scattered. The physical act of typing creates a bottleneck that forces your brain to slow down.


-


**Working memory offloading:** Typing requires you to hold an idea while you plan and execute keystrokes; speaking captures the thought before working memory drops it.


-


**Lower activation energy:** Talking has almost no startup cost compared to typing, helping users beat the blank-page freeze and task avoidance.


-


**Thought-capture speed:** Speaking at 150 words per minute matches a fast, associative train of thought much better than 40 WPM typing.


-


**Reduced editing tax:** Tools that auto-punctuate and remove filler words let you keep your momentum instead of fixing every sentence.


In the end,[voice dictation removes major friction](https://www.yaps.ai/blog/voice-dictation-adhd-neurodivergent) from the daily workflow as a productivity tool; it is not a medical treatment for ADHD, and users should consult a clinician for diagnosis or treatment.


Outside the office, the same benefits apply in everyday life. Students use speech-to-text to capture lecture notes in real time, bypassing the slow transcription that loses key points mid-class. For students with slow processing speed or dysgraphia, speaking an essay draft removes the physical bottleneck that stalls written output. And for anyone with ADHD, a quick voice memo on a phone captures a fleeting idea or to-do the moment it surfaces, before working memory drops it entirely.


## How Voice Recognition Works


You speak a sentence, and the text appears on screen instantly. Behind that moment, voice recognition moves through three stages. First, your microphone converts sound waves into digital samples; clean input and mic placement matter here. Next, AI models slice that audio into phonemes, compare them against learned speech patterns, and predict words, handling accents and word boundaries far more reliably than older rule-based systems. Finally, post-processing applies punctuation, capitalization, and filler-word removal using surrounding context. While older or built-in tools often take 700ms or more to handle this, advanced AI systems like Willow Voice complete the full pipeline in ~200 milliseconds.

## Getting Started With Voice Dictation When You Have ADHD


Switching to voice dictation feels awkward at first, especially if your brain is wired to expect immediate perfection from every tool you try. A few deliberate habits in the first week make the difference between giving up early and building a workflow that genuinely sticks.


1.


**Start in the app you use most.** Pick one place (your email inbox, your notes app, or your task manager) and dictate exclusively there for the first few days. Anchoring the habit to a familiar context lowers the barrier to starting.


2.


**Use a dedicated hotkey.** Assign a single keyboard shortcut to start and stop dictation. Removing the click-to-activate step cuts the friction that triggers avoidance.


3.


**Don't edit while you dictate.** Keep speaking even when a word comes out wrong. Stopping to fix errors mid-thought breaks the flow that makes voice dictation valuable for ADHD brains in the first place.


4.


**Speak in short bursts.** Aim for one idea per sentence. Short, punchy phrases are easier to correct if needed and train the recognition model faster than long, winding sentences.


5.


**Give it a week before judging accuracy.** Most AI dictation tools improve as they learn your vocabulary and speech patterns. Reserve judgment until you have at least five or six real sessions under your belt.

But that general-purpose design comes with a distinct architectural tradeoff.

Apple Dictation is best suited for casual Mac or iOS users with light, occasional dictation needs who are already in the Apple ecosystem and do not require professional-grade accuracy or cross-app consistency.
